target_pattern: Use tan with adjectives and adverbs, use tanto mucho and demasiado as adjective or adverb depending on context, and apply tan como and tanto como for quality and quantity comparisons.

cognitive_shift.english_trap: Using one generic so/much form without changing structure by function.
cognitive_shift.spanish_logic: Spanish separates degree and quantity. Tan modifies adjectives or adverbs, while tanto mucho demasiado can modify nouns with agreement or verbs as invariable adverbs.
target_pattern_formula: degree: tan plus adjective or adverb
adverbial amount: verb plus tanto or mucho or demasiado
quality comparison: tan plus adjective or adverb plus como
quantity or action comparison: tanto plus noun plus como or verb plus tanto como
natural_examples: Ella habla demasiado en las reuniones.

pattern_mutation.instructions: Transform each base sentence as instructed.
drills: Base: Este libro es tan interesante. -> change adjective to util.
Base: Maria corre tan rapido. -> change subject to plural ellos.
Base: Te quiero tanto. -> change pronoun to plural los quiero.
Base: Hay tantos problemas en el mundo. -> change noun to feminine singular gente.
Base: Hay tanta comida que no pudimos terminarla. -> change noun to plural flores.
Base: Hay muchas abejas en el jardin. -> change to masculine plural noun pajaros.
Base: Los hombres se quejan mucho. -> change subject to singular Juan.
Base: Ella habla demasiado. -> change subject to plural ellas.
Base: Compraste demasiadas cosas. -> change noun to masculine singular equipo.
Base: Maria es tan alta como su hermana. -> change adjective to organizada.
Base: Juan corre tan rapido como un atleta. -> change verb to nadar.
Base: Juan tiene tanto dinero como su amigo. -> change noun to plural libros.
Base: Los estudiantes tienen tantos libros como los profesores. -> change subject to singular el estudiante.
Base: Juan trabaja tanto como Maria. -> change subject to plural nosotros.
Base: Los ninos juegan tanto como estudian. -> change first verb to descansar.

prompts: So interesting book. (un libro tan interesante vs un libro tanto interesante)
I love you so much. (Te quiero tanto. vs Te quiero tan.)
There are so many people. (Hay tanta gente. vs Hay tan gente.)
They work a lot. (Trabajan mucho. vs Trabajan muchos.)
She talks too much. (Ella habla demasiado. vs Ella habla demasiada.)
As tall as her sister. (tan alta como su hermana vs tanta alta como su hermana)
As much money as you. (tanto dinero como tu vs tan dinero como tu)
As much as Maria works. (Juan trabaja tanto como Maria. vs Juan trabaja tan como Maria.)
Too many tasks. (demasiadas tareas vs demasiado tareas)
They run as fast as professionals. (Corren tan rapido como profesionales. vs Corren tanto rapido como profesionales.)

common_errors.why_it_happens: Direct transfer from English so many wording.
Degree and quantity categories are mixed.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Use tan with adjectives and adverbs.

common_errors.mistake: Missing agreement in tanto adjective forms
common_errors.correct_spanish: Match gender and number with the noun.
Use invariable adverb forms after verbs.

common_errors.mistake: Muchos used as adverb after verbs
common_errors.correct_spanish: Verb plus mucho for adverbial a lot.

common_errors.mistake: Tan como used for noun quantity comparison
common_errors.correct_spanish: Use tanto plus noun plus como.

common_errors.mistake: Tanto como used for adjective quality comparison
common_errors.correct_spanish: Use tan plus adjective or adverb plus como.
Keep full structure intact with final como phrase.

common_errors.mistake: Mucho used where excess meaning is intended
common_errors.why_it_happens: Mucho and demasiado treated as synonyms.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Use demasiado for too much or too many.

common_errors.why_it_happens: Fear of agreement and frame errors.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Use fixed templates and then swap vocabulary.
